note_on_method: Each venue page rests on the Naperville Park District's own location page for that park: the address, the amenity list and a single sentence about pickleball. To that are added the District's Park It page, which states that the courts at six named parks are outdoor, and the US Census address geocoder and OpenStreetMap for the county and the postcode. The operator is the Park District, not the City of Naperville. Where the District is silent, these pages record the silence.

slots.description:
Twelve pickleball courts at an athletic complex off Diehl Road on the north side of Naperville, the largest count published in the city.

The twelve is the Park District's own arithmetic in one sentence: "Nike Sports Complex has 4 dedicated pickleball courts and there are 8 lit tennis courts lined for pickleball; participants must provide their own nets". Four are pickleball courts in their own right. Eight are tennis courts carrying pickleball lines, and those eight are the ones the District calls lit. It says nothing about lights on the four dedicated courts, so this venue's lighting is recorded as unknown.

Ballfields, a cricket field, basketball courts, fitness stations, ice rinks, a synthetic field, picnic shelters and tennis courts share the ground. In January 2026 the District was awarded a $600,000 state grant for improvements it expects to build from late 2026 through 2028.
slots.getting_there:
288 W Diehl Road, Naperville, IL 60563, in DuPage County. The address resolves through OpenStreetMap rather than the US Census address file, which holds no record of it.

The District lists "Parking Spaces" among the amenities and publishes a parking map, the only one of the three published Naperville venues with one. A paved trail runs north-south with "a connection to the pickleball courts" and joins the sidewalks on Diehl Road and North Mill Street. Restrooms are listed, on a seasonal schedule the District asks you to check.
slots.what_to_expect:
Twelve courts is enough for a rotation, which makes this the one Naperville venue where turning up alone is a reasonable plan, provided you bring a net. The District's sentence ends "participants must provide their own nets", and nothing on the page exempts the four dedicated courts.

After dark the eight lined courts are the ones the District calls lit, and the four dedicated courts carry no lighting statement at all. The District publishes no hours, no price, no surface and nothing about when the courts are busy. It states on its Park It page that the courts are outdoor.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net?
faqs.a: Yes. The District's sentence ends "participants must provide their own nets", and it says nothing about nets being supplied on any of the twelve.
Not stated. The District publishes no price and no hours for these courts, so the fee is recorded here as unknown rather than as free.

slots.description:
Nine pickleball courts striped onto the tennis courts of a neighbourhood park on the south side of Naperville, unlit, on a surface the Park District names and explains.

The count is the District's own total: "The tennis courts have striping for a total of 9 pickleball courts." They are lines rather than courts of their own, and the District's other sentence, "Ranchview Park has 6 unlit courts using tennis nets", supplies the lighting answer in one word.

The surface paragraph is what makes this page unusual. "The tennis/pickleball courts have a modular plastic tile system to ensure continuous operation and minimize maintenance. These tennis courts have a history of traditional tennis court color coatings failing prematurely due to the amount of moisture emitted by the roof of the concrete reservoir below."
slots.getting_there:
1727 Ranchview Drive, Naperville, IL 60565. The US Census address geocoder matched "1727 RANCHVIEW DR, NAPERVILLE, IL, 60565" at house-number level and placed it in DuPage County, in the incorporated place Naperville city.

The District lists "Parking Spaces" among the park's amenities and says nothing more: no map, no capacity, no fee. It lists no restrooms here, and that absence is recorded as a silence rather than a no.
slots.what_to_expect:
Nine unlit courts, so daylight play, with room for four games at once. The District publishes no hours, no price and nothing about when the courts are used.

Nets are the thing to plan for, because the District's page says two different things about them. One sentence reads "Ranchview Park has 6 unlit courts using tennis nets". The next reads "3 courts on the west side use the tennis nets, 6 courts on the east side require patrons to bring their own nets." Neither is resolved, so the net answer is recorded as unknown. Bring a portable net and you are covered on either side. Without one you have three courts at most, at tennis-net height.

The courts are outdoor on the District's Park It page.

faqs.q: How many courts are there, six or nine?
faqs.a: Nine. The District's page prints two numbers: "Ranchview Park has 6 unlit courts using tennis nets" and "The tennis courts have striping for a total of 9 pickleball courts." The nine is its own stated total, made up of three courts on the west side and six on the east. All nine are lines on the tennis courts.

slots.description:
Four pickleball courts on the tennis courts of a neighbourhood park in the far south-west of Naperville, unlit, with the nets already there.

The Park District's whole pickleball record for this park is one sentence: "Ashbury Park has 4 unlit courts using tennis nets". Four courts is enough for two games at once. "Unlit" is a stated negative rather than a silence. "Using tennis nets" means there is a net on the court when you arrive, a tennis net at tennis height.

The District also lists a ballfield, fishing, ponds, parking spaces and trails. A multi-use trail runs east-west from Ashbury Greenway to Book Road and along the shoreline of the pond on the south side of the park.
slots.getting_there:
1740 Conan Doyle Road, Naperville, IL 60564. The US Census address geocoder matched "1740 CONAN DOYLE RD, NAPERVILLE, IL, 60564" at house-number level and placed it in Will County, in the incorporated place Naperville city. Naperville straddles two counties on the Census's own answers, and this is the published venue on the Will side.

The District lists "Parking Spaces" among the amenities and publishes no map, capacity or fee. It lists no restrooms here, which is recorded as unknown rather than as a no.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four courts, unlit, nets in place. Two games can run side by side, and play ends with the daylight on the District's own word.

This is the simplest venue in Naperville to turn up at, because there is nothing to bring. "Using tennis nets" also means the courts are lines on tennis courts, so they exist only as long as the tennis courts are free.

The District publishes no hours, no price and nothing about when the courts are busy. It states on its Park It page that the courts are outdoor. On Ranchview Park's page it remarks that "The tennis courts at Ashbury Park have a cushioned overlay system over asphalt", a statement about the tennis courts made on another park's page and not published here as this venue's pickleball surface.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net?
faqs.a: No. The courts are "using tennis nets", so a net is there when you arrive, a tennis net at tennis height.
Not stated. The District publishes no price and no hours, so the fee is recorded as unknown rather than as free.
